Everybody else, from conference leader Georgia to — wait, is this right? — conference co-leader Kentucky, can claim they beat somebody who beat somebody who beat somebody who beat the biggest dog (or dawg) in the yard. item.title: Tributes pour in for ESPN Radio legend Dan ‘The Duke’ Davis
item.description: Credit: ESPN ESPN Radio legend Dan Davis, known as “The Duke” by friends and coworkers, has died at the age of 84. Davis was a founding member of ESPN Radio when it launched in 1992 and spent two decades as a SportsCenter update reporter. Before joining the Worldwide Leader, Davis had already made his mark as the man on the call for Doug Flutie’s “Hail Mary” pass for Boston College against Miami in 1984 on WRKO/ABC Radio. Boston College Football mourns the passing of Dan Davis, whose voice became part of the program’s history. From calling Doug Flutie’s iconic Hail Mary in 1984 to dozens of BC Football broadcasts, his legacy will forever be part of The Heights. Davis’ call of Doug Flutie’s famous Hail Mary in 1984, courtesy of WRKO/ABC Radio — Boston College Football (@BCFootball) October 21, 2026 At ESPN, several prominent figures from behind the mic shared their appreciation and remembrances of Davis. “What a voice he had. What a great man he was,” said Mike Golic Sr. “I was happy to call him friend.” The Golics then played Davis’s fantastic Hail Mary call. “What a great call by Dan,” Golic Sr. said. “Still one of the favorite calls in the Boston area. … An incredible man with an incredible voice. 84 years old he passed away. Certainly, there are so many people who are still at ESPN Radio or had worked at ESPN Radio who are passing around texts now reliving our Dan ‘The Duke’ Davis moments. He was a special, special man.” RIP to an @ESPNRadio legend, Dan “The Duke” Davis https://t.co/kPjArUkd9X — The Golics (@thegolics) October 21, 2026 Scott Van Pelt also paid tribute to Davis, referencing a recurring bit he had on his ESPN Radio show alongside Ryen Russillo, where Davis would read out hip hop lyrics as stoic spoken word to delightful results . Of all the things we did on SVP & Russillo, The Duke raps was an all time favorite. Dan “The Duke” Davis was the best. Not sure he got it initially, but @ryenarussillo got him to buy in and The Duke made it memorable. RIP to a legend. Love to his family and friends. https://t.co/H8UVEQczrH — Scott Van Pelt (@notthefakeSVP) October 21, 2026 Other former coworkers shared their own memories of Davis after ESPN shared the news over social media. Working with The Duke was one of the great honors and pleasures of my radio days. As great an update man as there ever was .. and one heck of a radio call on the Flutie Hail Mary pass for BC. Prayers to all those who were lucky enough to have Dan in their lives. The best!! — MikeTirico (@miketirico) October 21, 2026 The Duke was a legend. — Stanford Steve (@StanfordSteve82) October 21, 2026 He was one of one! From the moment the radio side of @espn began he and many others were in what we’d have to describe as a very large closet. In those days I’d occasionally fly in for some CFB Halftime and post game studio work. He’s call of the Flutiento Phelan Catch in 84’will live forever @BCFootball RIP Dan a true legend that loved his job and lived to his fullest. — Tim

It’s nowhere near complete – the hope is to accommodate a couple of thousand fans in it by March and have it up and running next season – but the structure is taking shape. • Wrexham shouldn't push the panic button yet despite challenge facing Phil Parkinson • What Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac need to do to keep Wrexham's 'heart' after emotional exit Its significance is becoming clearer, too. Perched on a hill which is one of the conurbation’s highest points, it dominates Newcastle and can be seen from most vantage points in the area. Wrexham was a significant location in the early years of the Industrial Revolution. As a market town, it was already a nexus between markets and suppliers, and by happy geological coincidence, that status was enhanced as factories and trade exploded in the Nineteenth Century. • Wrexham needs to face up to 'vital' challenge after perfect Southampton win • Wrexham's Southampton revenge was perfect after team let Phil Parkinson down Slate from north west Wales, coal from across the region and the produce of the world’s first steel works, built on the fringes of Wrexham passed through the town along with the very ground our ancestors trod. When Premier League clubs Nottingham Forest and Chelsea played at The Racecourse last season, they each caused logistical problems by arriving the day before with an entire busload of equipment for their support staff, which they left in the narrow corridors of the stadium, making it difficult for staff to negotiate their way around their place of work! Now we’ll have a stand to be proud of, a statement which spreads our story even further, and room to accommodate more fans and bigger opponents. As long as that pesky old Godzilla doesn’t turn up before the concrete sets.

item.title: Tyson Fury unveils three sparring partners to prepare for Anthony Joshua
item.description: Tyson Fury has unveiled his sparring partners as he prepares to box Anthony Joshua , with familiar faces in tow. Fury and Joshua will finally square off on 11 December , after nearly a decade of calls for the heavyweight fight to be made . The Britons will meet at Cardiff’s Principality Stadium, with the bout streaming live on Netflix. In preparation for the grudge match, Fury has enlisted the help of compatriot Joe Joyce , controversial US star Jarrell Miller, and Russia’s Aleksei Dronov. Tyson Fury at the launch press conference for his fight with Anthony Joshua (Getty) Fury, 38, shared an AI image of the trio alongside himself and coach Sugarhill Steward, with every one of them in Viking gear. “Clan war lords instead of spartans, we coming dec 11,” Fury wrote on Thursday. British fans may know Joyce for his fights with Daniel Dubois, Derek Chisora, Joseph Parker and Zhilei Zhang. The Olympic silver medalist handed Dubois the first loss of his career, stopping him in 2020 before doing the same to Parker two years later. However, those wins gave way to back-to-back KOs by Zhang, and a points loss to Chisora later. Meanwhile, Miller was famously due to box Joshua in the latter’s US debut in 2019, only to be pulled from the fight after failing a drug test. “AJ” went on to be knocked out by Andy Ruiz Jr. Miller, who failed another test in 2020, suffered a late stoppage by Dubois in 2023 and battled Ruiz to a draw the following year. Joe Joyce has been out of form in recent years (PA) And Dronov is the least known of Fury’s training partners, a former gold medalist at the youth Olympics and amateur youth world championships. The Russian, 24, is 12-0 as a professional with 10 KOs. On Wednesday, Fury had written: “Another beautiful day in camp fury, 10 good rounds sparring with 2 guys, Camp is my happy place & I’m as happy as ever at 38 years old. “Very good vibes in camp, my 3rd fight camp of 2026, Feeling fantastic as good as ever, I’m ready to become 3 times heavyweight champion of the world, in the mighty name of Jesus christ.”

item.title: Sri Lanka make 430 to beat England after Brook's 202
item.description: Brook's previous highest score in ODIs was 136 not out, also against Sri Lanka [Getty Images] One-day international tri-series, Rawalpindi England 429-4 (50 overs): Brook 202, Root 69, Jacks 66* Sri Lanka 430-8 (49.5 overs): Rathnayake 130, Avishka 97, Shanaka 97 Sri Lanka won by two wickets Scorecard Harry Brook's first double century by an England batter in a one-day international was not enough to prevent his team being stunned by Sri Lanka, who pulled off a remarkable chase of 430 in Rawalpindi. Brook passed Ben Stokes' previous England best score of 182 and posted the fastest ODI double hundred, off 114 balls, in his astonishing 202. In clobbering the 14th double-hundred in a men's one-day international and the 12th highest individual score, Brook lifted England to 429-4 – at halfway the highest total made in a one-day international in Pakistan. But Sri Lanka, who chose to bat second, were not deterred, even when they were reduced to 24-2. They set about completing the second-highest successful chase in ODI history. Pavan Rathnayake made a sublime 130, while Aviksha Fernando and Dasun Shanaka both added 97. With Jofra Archer rested for the tri-series and leg-spinner Adil Rashid left out of this match for tactical reasons, England's bowling was woeful. Sam Curran conceded 103 runs from his nine overs. Up with the required rate throughout their innings, Sri Lanka needed 109 from the final 10 overs and were able to absorb the losses of Rathnayake and Shanaka. Sri Lanka needed eight off the final over, sent down by Josh Tongue, who was pinpoint with his accuracy to bowl Dinuth Wellalage and Eshan Malinga with successive deliveries. But in a sensational finish, Janith Liyanage, the man bowling when Brook reached 200, would not be denied. With six needed from two balls, Liyanage pummelled Tongue's penultimate delivery of the match down the ground for a match-winning maximum, sparking joyous of celebrations by the Sri Lankans. One of the most incredible one-day internationals ever played ended with an aggregate of 847 runs, behind only a match total of 872 when South Africa chased 435 to beat Australia in 2006. The total of 123 boundaries across both innings - 93 fours and 30 sixes - is also a record in ODIs. England floored in astonishing ODI How did England lose this game? At halfway, when Brook left the field arm-in-arm with Will Jacks, the thought of Sri Lanka even getting close to their target seemed highly fanciful. Yet, Sri Lankan captain Kusal Mendis' decision to chase proved inspired, despite the way his team were dismantled by Brook. Ultimately, Sri Lanka put the conditions – and Brook's knock – into context, helped by an England team who wilted under the pressure. item.content:encoded: Brook's previous highest score in ODIs was 136 not out, also against Sri Lanka [Getty Images] One-day international tri-series, Rawalpindi England 429-4 (50 overs): Brook 202, Root 69, Jacks 66* Sri Lanka 430-8 (49.5 overs): Rathnayake 130, Avishka 97, Shanaka 97 Sri Lanka won by two wickets Scorecard Harry Brook's first double century by an England batter in a one-day international was not enough to prevent his team being stunned by Sri Lanka, who pulled off a remarkable chase of 430 in Rawalpindi. Brook passed Ben Stokes' previous England best score of 182 and posted the fastest ODI double hundred, off 114 balls, in his astonishing 202. In clobbering the 14th double-hundred in a men's one-day international and the 12th highest individual score, Brook lifted England to 429-4 – at halfway the highest total made in a one-day international in Pakistan. But Sri Lanka, who chose to bat second, were not deterred, even when they were reduced to 24-2. They set about completing the second-highest successful chase in ODI history. Pavan Rathnayake made a sublime 130, while Aviksha Fernando and Dasun Shanaka both added 97. With Jofra Archer rested for the tri-series and leg-spinner Adil Rashid left out of this match for tactical reasons, England's bowling was woeful. Sam Curran conceded 103 runs from his nine overs. Up with the required rate throughout their innings, Sri Lanka needed 109 from the final 10 overs and were able to absorb the losses of Rathnayake and Shanaka. Sri Lanka needed eight off the final over, sent down by Josh Tongue, who was pinpoint with his accuracy to bowl Dinuth Wellalage and Eshan Malinga with successive deliveries. But in a sensational finish, Janith Liyanage, the man bowling when Brook reached 200, would not be denied. With six needed from two balls, Liyanage pummelled Tongue's penultimate delivery of the match down the ground for a match-winning maximum, sparking joyous of celebrations by the Sri Lankans. One of the most incredible one-day internationals ever played ended with an aggregate of 847 runs, behind only a match total of 872 when South Africa chased 435 to beat Australia in 2006. The total of 123 boundaries across both innings - 93 fours and 30 sixes - is also a record in ODIs. England floored in astonishing ODI How did England lose this game? At halfway, when Brook left the field arm-in-arm with Will Jacks, the thought of Sri Lanka even getting close to their target seemed highly fanciful. Yet, Sri Lankan captain Kusal Mendis' decision to chase proved inspired, despite the way his team were dismantled by Brook. Ultimately, Sri Lanka put the conditions – and Brook's knock – into context, helped by an England team who wilted under the pressure. They were hampered by the dew, another factor in Sri Lanka's decision to bat second. England made mistakes in the field and their bowlers struggled to grip the ball. Without Archer, they lacked a death bowler. And, with less then a year to go until the World Cup, England showed no composure as the game began to run away from them. For as well as Brook batted, his tactics will come into question. Too much faith was placed in Curran, whose 103-2 are the most expensive figures returned by an England bowler in an ODI. Gus Atkinson opened the bowling and sent down just seven overs of his allotted 10 and Tongue, who almost rescued the game, was only into his ninth. This tri-series is designed to replicate the tournament conditions England will face at the World Cup in southern Africa. Two games in they are without a win and facing the prospect of needing to beat Pakistan in Lahore on Sunday to stay in the competition.

Based on the theme “Fans,” the finalist designs captured different expressions of Atlético’s identity, and it was up to the fans to decide which would come to life as Manto da Massa 2026/27. If Bane and Jalen Suggs stay healthy this season, Black will be a super sub for Orlando, but he should be viewed as a de facto sixth starter. Black’s agents will likely use the extensions signed by Golden State Warriors guard Brandin Podziemski (five years, $110 million) and Oklahoma City Thunder guard Cason Wallace (five years, $139 million) as the starting point for negotiations next offseason. He might not reach the heights of Detroit Pistons wing Ausar Thompson or Utah Jazz guard Keyonte George (five years, $155 million), but a $20-plus million annual average salary seems like the bare minimum he’ll get if he maintains his level of production from last season. It could be tough for Orlando to fit that type of contract moving forward without shedding salary elsewhere. Franz Wagner, Paolo Banchero and Bane will combine to earn roughly $131.5 million in 2027-28. Add in Suggs ($29.6 million) and Wendell Carter Jr. ($19.6 million), and the Magic’s starting five alone will push them over the projected $176 million salary cap by nearly $5 million. The Magic are currently projected to be about $20.3 million below the luxury-tax line, $29 million below the first apron and $42 million below the second apron in 2027-28, but they have only eight players under contract for that season at the moment. Since a veteran-minimum contract is projected to be north of $2.6 million, even filling out the rest of their roster with min deals would cost Orlando more than $15 million. The Magic haven’t paid a single dollar in luxury tax since Dwight Howard’s heyday in the late 2000s. They’re more than $17 million above this year’s tax line, for now which would result in a tax bill north of $30 million. If they stay in the tax this year and in two of the ensuing three seasons, they’d then become subject to the far more punitive repeater tax rate. They’d need to go on at least one deep playoff run to justify that kind of spending. Otherwise, they’ll likely have to trade one of their starters (Suggs?) if they hope to retain Black next offseason. A Missed Window? When the Magic traded for Bane, it looked like the perfect time for them to strike. Boston Celtics forward Jayson Tatum and Indiana Pacers point guard Tyrese Haliburton both tore their Achilles tendons during the 2025 playoffs and figured to miss most or all of the 2025-26 campaign. That left a power vacuum at the top of the Eastern Conference. The New York Knicks and Cleveland Cavaliers looked like the clear class of the East heading into last season, but the Magic were a trendy dark-horse pick to at least make it to the conference finals. Instead, Wagner missed more than half the season, and their offense continued to sputter even after the addition of Bane. The Magic squeaked into the playoffs as the No. 8 seed after smashing the Charlotte Hornets in the play-in tournament, and they put a real scare into the top-seeded Pistons. But after falling short, they fired head coach Jamahl Mosley and replaced him with San Antonio Spurs assistant Sean Sweeney. Sweeney arrived in Orlando with a sterling reputation, but he might be facing an uphill battle with this Magic roster. After all, the East underwent a drastic overhaul this offseason, which has the conference looking far more loaded than it was in 2025-26. The Philadelphia 76ers added LeBron James and Jaylen Brown. The Miami Heat traded for Giannis Antetokounmpo. The Toronto Raptors reacquired Kawhi Leonard. The Celtics landed Paul George in exchange for Brown. The Pistons swapped out Tobias Harris and Isaiah Stewart for John Collins and Isaiah Joe. The Cavaliers acquired Peyton Watson. And the Atlanta Hawks, who beat the Magic in both teams’ season opener on Wednesday, got Lu Dort and Aaron Wiggins from the Oklahoma City Thunder. No one should overreact to one loss, particularly in the season opener. After all, the Celtics started 0-3 last season only to finish 56-26. However, the Magic’s next five games are against the Minnesota Timberwolves, the Knicks, the Raptors (twice) and the Celtics. Their schedule lightens up significantly after that—a four-game road trip against the Phoenix Suns, Golden State Warriors, Sacramento Kings and Utah Jazz could be just what the doctor ordered—but the NBA’s new draft-lottery system should mean fewer easy wins against tanking teams this season. Even if the Magic do have to start breaking apart their core after this season, they should be able to get a positive return on whomever they decide to trade, particularly if it’s Banchero or Wagner. They might not be able to recoup what they gave up for Bane, but the apron era spares no victim. Once your roster gets too expensive, you’re forced into difficult choices such as these. This year could wind up being the end of an era for this Magic squad. Given the increased competition they face in the East, it’s possible that their title window has closed just as quickly as it opened. This time, there was a free rusher, but Purdy didn’t find his outlet receiver out of the backfield. Instead, he attempted to scramble at the last minute. I’m more inclined to believe the Kyle Shanahan-led offense, with a week of practice to prepare without Mike Evans, will be well-equipped to score. I’d also argue the pass-catching corps heading into Week 7 without Evans is still better than what the offense trotted out on a weekly basis in 2025—not to mention the improved offensive line and quarterback. The panic centers around Evans and his potential absence. It comes off as a prisoner-of-the-moment move, wanting to trade for a wideout. The team could essentially give Evans close to three weeks off so he can recover ahead of Week 9 against the Raiders. The thought of adding to a strength makes sense on the surface. It’s part of the reason the Niners should be open to adding to the defensive line. However, the players being floated around don’t move the needle enough to warrant moving draft picks. They would if the 49ers were going to miss the wideouts currently injured for the rest of the season, but that’s not the case. Christian Kirk practiced in full on Wednesday. He appears set to make his debut. Let’s use Colts receiver Josh Downs as an example, a player we highlighted as a trade target earlier this month . Downs runs 70% of his routes from the slot. That’s where Kirk figures to line up. Just last week against the Titans, Downs caught a few underneath throws, couldn’t hold onto a contested catch against Isaiah Oliver- yes, that Isaiah Oliver- and also dropped a wide-open pass. He caught a 23-yarder that was a deep pass over the middle. But nothing about his game suggests Kirk or any of the other wideouts couldn’t do the same with the same opportunity. Downs currently has a 20.6% target share. He wouldn’t sniff that number on a team that throws the ball to Evans 23.5% of the time, George Kittle 21.7% of the time, and Christian McCaffrey 21.1% of the time. Downs, or any wideout under consideration, isn’t on the same level as those three. Between Kirk, Demarcus Robinson, and Deebo Samuel—not to mention De’Zhaun Stribling—the 49ers already have a bit of a logjam in their receiver room. But it is the Niners, and the primary concern, per every year ever, is health. Shanahan can weather the storm without a week of Evans. After all, no offense has generated a higher EPA per pass or success rate through the air than San Francisco. The receiver room should be as close to healthy coming out of the bye week, making the need for a receiver moot with Robinson and Samuel back. Where would the targets go to Downs, or Brian Thomas, or pick your receiver? A rental, like Downs, makes less sense. If the 49ers are going to swing, it should look more like Bryce Eldridge than a guy who blends in with the rest of the Triple-A lineup — looking at you, Shay Whitcomb. Like Eldridge, that player needs to be a legitimate impact player. If you’re looking for a playmaker, call the Saints to see if Chris Olave is for sale. Check with the Jets to see if Garrett Wilson is available. Those are game-changers who complement Evans and will be around beyond this season. Even then, you’re stunting Stribling’s growth and basically pulling the plug on Ricky Pearsall. From a team-building perspective, the 49ers have everything they need at receiver in-house. The reason the Niners will win the Super Bowl is already on the roster. We’ve been watching him for six weeks. It’s the receiver who has the highest EPA per target in the league. They already went out and got Brock a WR1. Now, it’s about keeping him healthy and ensuring he’s available late in the season. Fact or fiction: Fiction, easily. If the 49ers are calling the Colts, Downs should be third on the list. DeForest Buckner is No. 1, with Quenton Nelson 1b. You know how to improve your offense? Go out and get the left guard with the fifth-most impact blocks of any player this year who hasn’t allowed a sack and has the same pressure percentage as Trent Williams. Now that’s a rental that makes sense. Downs or a 6-time All-Pro who makes your run game better, gives your quarterback more time to throw, and allows your wideouts more time to get open? Tough choice. Buckner doesn’t need any explanation. But if the Niners make a trade, it should build on their strength. This season, that’s in the trenches on both sides of the ball.

item.title: USA to host women's football Club World Cup in 2028 - FIFA
item.description: FIFA's sign at the entrance of the world football's governing body headquarters in Zurich (Fabrice COFFRINI) The United States will host the inaugural women's football Club World Cup in 2028, FIFA announced Thursday. "The decision was taken in view of its experience in organising FIFA tournaments, the maturity of its infrastructure and services and the level of stakeholder interest in women's football in the country," world football's governing body said. The US has a proven track record of staging large sporting events, notably co-hosting the men's World Cup earlier this year. The first-ever women's Club World Cup will be staged from January 5-30, 2028. It will bring together 19 top-tier clubs from all six continental confederations. The AFC (Asia), CAF (Africa), CONCACAF (North America) and CONMEBOL (South America) will be represented by three clubs apiece at the competition, one team will fly the flag for the OFC (Oceania) and six of Europe's best sides will represent UEFA. Seven clubs have already secured their berths at the tournament: Arsenal (England), Club America Femenil (Mexico), Barcelona (Spain), Gotham (United States), Naegohyang (North Korea), Corinthians (Brazil) and Wuhan Jiangda (China). "These seven clubs, and a dozen more, will come together to show the strength and depth of women's club football to a global audience," said FIFA chief women's football officer Sarai Bareman. "They will have the opportunity to tell their story, expand their fan base and represent their club on the world stage. They have thoroughly earned this opportunity to be part of history in the United States." FIFA said the introduction of the tournament marked "a major milestone for the professionalisation and global expansion of the women's club game, giving elite club sides a true world stage to compete on every four years". Initially slated for 2026, FIFA pushed the inaugural tournament back by two years so it enjoys a clear window following the 2027 women's World Cup and ahead of the 2028 Summer Olympics in Los Angeles. lp/dmc

item.title: Jimmie Johnson on the NASCAR business world: "It's a war"
item.description: Motorsport photo As part of the Autosport Business Exchange in New York this week, NASCAR legend Jimmie Johnson was a guest speaker where he discussed his career as a driver, and also his transition into the role of team owner. Johnson competed full-time at the top level of the sport between 2002 and 2020, winning 83 races and a record-tying seven championships as a Hendrick Motorsports driver. After competing in IMSA, IndyCar, and even the 24 Hours of Le Mans, Johnson has taken on a new role as a team owner at Legacy Motor Club. Going into it, he joked that he just "didn't want to be the athlete that screws it up -- thinks he's a business guy and makes mistakes." When Johnson joined the organization, they rebranded to Legacy and have since added an impressive list of investors . In 2027, they will expand with a third chartered Cup entry , and have hired both Josh Berry and Riley Herbst to race alongside Erik Jones . They became a Toyota-backed team in 2024, and have made several notable hires on the competition side over the past year. Lindsay Czarniak, and Jimmie Johnson Lindsay Czarniak, and Jimmie Johnson "There's still a long road ahead," continued Johnson. "We'll see what happens. But, you know, I've been mentored throughout my career and have really tried to set up a structure where people I really trust are helping me grow and evolve in this space. And, you know, thankful for the journey, learning so much every single day. "I'm also a competitor at heart. And I have to say, I never appreciated the race within the race. I had the great fortune of holding the steering wheel and understanding that competitive lane. But, man, the commercial competitive space and fighting for sponsorship, fighting for personnel, it's a war. It's a whole different race. Johnson noted how difficult it was to understand the business and competition aspect as a driver as "you live in this one-dimensional world." However, he certainly gained a newfound appreciation for what it takes to run a successful team after stepping into the role of owner himself. "When you look at your competition department, your business ops, and how all of that, you know, fits together and how harmonious it all needs to be for success," said Johnson. "You know, within success, I firmly believe in this -- it's people. We're now approaching 215 people within Legacy as we expand to our third program for next year. It's a lot of babysitting. It's a lot of layers. It's a lot of stuff. And it's all people. And trying to have people bond and find a common goal and work together is quite the challenge." item.title: Dortmund launch initiative to keep fans away from phones during games
item.description: ILLUSTRATION - A young boy uses a mobile phone. Children in the United Kingdom under age 16 will be banned from social media in a “big moment for our country,” British Prime Minister Keir Starmer said on Monday. (is associated with: «Dortmund launch initiative to keep fans away from phones during games») Antti Aimo-Koivisto/Lehtikuva/dpa Borussia Dortmund want to encourage fans to put away their smartphones while watching games at the stadium and are releasing a new feature on their official app. The "Fan Mode" can be activated in the club's app on game days. When the feature is on, the app tracks the amount of time the screen is locked and fans earn points for every minute they go without using their phones. During half-time, fans can use their devices, but must reactivate "Fan Mode" for the second half. The final whistle marks the end of the points-earning period. Participants with the most points can win prizes, including autographed Dortmund jerseys and gift vouchers for the fan shop. According to the club, nearly two-thirds of football fans in the stands regularly use their phones during matches. "More and more fans are annoyed by selfies, streaming, and social media in the stands," reads a club statement about the new feature, which will be available from Saturday’s Bundesliga match against Eintracht Frankfurt. "Leave your smartphone in your pocket and enjoy the game with all your senses," the statement urged.

item.title: BBC to show Cray Wanderers v Stockport & Altrincham v Notts County
item.description: Moss Lane will stage Altrincham's attempt to cause an 18th FA Cup upset against a league side [Getty Images] Non-league clubs Altrincham and Cray Wanderers will stage the BBC's two chosen FA Cup first-round ties next month. National League club Alty host former winners Notts County at Moss Lane on Saturday, 7 November (17:15 GMT, BBC Two/iPlayer). Bromley-based Cray, from the seventh-tier Isthmian League, and making their first appearance at this stage of the competition, will host League One leaders Stockport County the following day (Sunday, 8 November 14:15 GMT, BBC 2/iPlayer). They reached this stage by beating Bedford Town on penalties in Tuesday's replay after a 2-2 draw. Cray are recognised as London's oldest football club, pre-dating the FA Cup itself, which was first played in 1872. Tkachuk and his brother Matthew, a star winger for the Panthers, faced criticism over their “Wingmen” podcast, while Brady’s decision to attend a White House celebration following the U.S. men’s Olympic gold medal also drew backlash. Speculation about Tkachuk’s future in Ottawa intensified late last season. At the team’s season-ending news conference in April, he acknowledged the rumors had become a distraction and insisted, “I have been fully committed to this team.” Less than two months later, Tkachuk was traded to Florida, where his brother has won two Stanley Cup championships. “I’ve talked about it a lot that, you know, there’s professional reasons, personal reasons why I wasn’t going to re-sign here, and a lot of those things have remained private between (Senators general manager Steve Staios) and I,” Tkachuk said. “It’s going to remain private. Season-ticket holder Neil Kennelly and his son Nolan both wore Tkachuk jerseys with an X taped over the captain’s C. On the back, Nolan had covered Tkachuk’s name with the words “Wingmen is trash.” “I’m not going to say I was crazy angry or surprised, but you know what? He doesn’t want to be here, don’t let the door hit you on the way out,” Neil Kennelly said. “We want people who want to be here.” A group of four friends had similar perspectives. All four had Tkachuk jerseys and had changed the name plate. “He says he’s a big boy, but his brother and dad made the decision for him,” said Phil Grant. item.title: Tigers rumors: Detroit mentioned as Tarik Skubal free agency suitor, but there’s a catch
item.description: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images Tigers rumors: Detroit mentioned as Tarik Skubal free agency suitor, but there’s a catch appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Dodgers made a massive mid-season move in an effort to win a third straight World Series. The Dodgers acquired Tarik Skubal from the Detroit Tigers midseason. The Dodgers were eliminated from the playoffs in the NLCS, and Skubal is set to be a free agent. Dodgers teammates have already begun to lobby for Skubal to return to the team. There are plenty of teams expected to be in pursuit of the ace pitcher , but one of them could be his former employer, according to Mark Feinsand of MLB.com. “Although Detroit made the difficult decision to move Skubal before the Trade Deadline, the pitcher said he “would love to return” to the Tigers as a free agent. Could the Tigers shock the world by trading Skubal for three prospects in early August, then bringing him back with a monster free-agent deal only a few months later? It seems unlikely that the Tigers will get involved in a bidding war, so if Skubal is determined to get every last dollar, it probably won’t result in a return to the Motor City,” Feinsand wrote. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Tigers were not able to come to an agreement on a long-term deal with Skubal, leading to his ultimate trade. If Skubal is willing to take a discount to return to the Tigers, then a deal may come, but if not, he could be looking elsewhere. There is also the timing of the deal. The collective bargaining agreement between MLB and the MLBPA expires on December 1 . This means owners may not want to sign an agreement before then, but players may be motivated to get deals done in case of changes. Regardless of what the rules will be in place, many teams will want the services of Skubal.

However, convincing victories do not automatically establish championship quality, particularly when opponents vary in talent, experience and defensive strength. The Stanford game produced another dominant performance, with Notre Dame winning 58-7 before traveling to BYU. That road matchup offered a more demanding test, and the result showed why evaluating a team’s strength requires more than counting victories or examining final scores. item.title: Reds’ World Series champion dies at 63
item.description: The Cincinnati Reds are mourning the loss of former MLB first baseman and 1990 World Series champion Todd Benzinger, who died Wednesday at the age of 63. The Cincinnati Reds are saddened by the passing of former first baseman and 1990 World Series champion Todd Benzinger. Todd will be remembered with great affection and gratitude for his place in one of the most memorable chapters in Reds history. Our deepest condolences go out to his family, friends, former teammates and all who knew and loved him. — Cincinnati Reds (@Reds) October 22, 2026 The Reds announced his passing Thursday, remembering Benzinger for his role on one of the most celebrated teams in franchise history. MORE: 2026 World Series will be just second of its kind in past 100 years Benzinger was part of a historic Reds championship APRIL 1989: Cincinnati Reds’ player Todd Benzinger swings. Reds 3 Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Benzinger joined Cincinnati in 1989 and spent three seasons with the Reds through 1991. He became an important member of the 1990 club, which went wire-to-wire in winning the National League West before sweeping the heavily favored Oakland Athletics in the World Series. The 1990 Reds remain one of the most memorable teams in franchise history. Cincinnati finished the World Series with a four-game sweep, winning Games 1 through 4 and capturing the organization’s fifth championship. Benzinger played in all four games of the World Series, including starts at first base in Games 3 and 4. He became permanently connected to the championship when he caught the final out of the series in foul territory near first base, securing Cincinnati’s sweep of Oakland. A lasting place in Reds history OCTOBER 19, 1990: Todd Benzinger signs autographs before starting Game 3. 1990 Cincy Reds 21 Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Benzinger’s MLB career began with Boston in 1987 before he moved to Cincinnati. He ultimately played nine seasons in the majors, also spending time with Kansas City, Los Angeles, and San Francisco. He finished his career with 924 games, 66 home runs and 376 RBIs. His place in Reds history, however, will forever be defined by the 1990 championship. That team featured stars including Barry Larkin, Eric Davis, Chris Sabo, Paul O’Neill and Jose Rijo, along with the famous “Nasty Boys” bullpen. Cincinnati’s unexpected championship remains one of the defining accomplishments in franchise history. The Reds expressed their condolences to Benzinger’s family, friends, former teammates and everyone who knew him. No cause of death has been publicly released. For Reds fans, Benzinger will always be remembered as one of the players who helped deliver the franchise’s 1990 championship — and as the man who caught the final out that completed the historic sweep. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

The Chicago Bulls opened their 2026-27 regular season with a humiliating 135-92 loss to the Kawhi Leonard-led Toronto Raptors on Wednesday night, with Josh Giddey ’s previously undisclosed wrist injury potentially contributing to one of the worst performances of his NBA career. Following Chicago’s 43-point home loss, Giddey revealed that he suffered a left wrist injury during the preseason and underwent an MRI. The 24-year-old guard indicated that he would have to manage the injury moving forward. K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network shared Giddey’s revelation Wednesday via X, formerly known as Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Josh Giddey, asked by @SamSmithHoops about wrap he had on left wrist, said it happened during first preseason game and he had an MRI and it’s something he’s gonna have to play through for awhile.” Johnson also highlighted an interesting detail regarding Chicago’s handling of the injury. “Giddey hasn’t been listed on injury report” The revelation raises questions about whether the injury affected Giddey’s shooting during Chicago’s season opener, although the guard did not directly attribute his struggles to the wrist issue. Josh Giddey’s shooting struggles highlight Bulls’ disastrous season opener Giddey finished Wednesday’s loss with just two points, seven rebounds and six assists while committing five turnovers across 24 minutes. The Australian guard shot an abysmal 1-for-10 from the field, including 0-for-4 from 3-point range and 0-for-2 from the free-throw line. His performance marked a disastrous beginning to the campaign, particularly as Chicago looks to establish a new identity under head coach Tiago Splitter. The Bulls struggled to contain Toronto throughout the contest, suffering a lopsided defeat against a Raptors team led by Leonard. While Giddey’s wrist injury could help explain his offensive difficulties, Chicago will need significantly better production from its starting guard moving forward. The Bulls (0-1) will look to rebound from their embarrassing opener when they travel to face the Milwaukee Bucks (0-1) on Friday at 4 p.m. ET. item.title: Trump’s Fifa peace prize was a sham. A reimagined award can still have meaning | Leander Schaerlaeckens
item.description: The first awarding marked the apex of Gianni Infantino’s hubris. A new version could highlight the good in the world of soccer Sign up for our free newsletter here Poor Fifa peace prize. Unloved, unliked, mocked, tainted by association with its first winner. And now demoted, too, after Fifa president Gianni Infantino dumped the thing on the global governing body’s “social responsibility committee” to look after. To redeem it, rather than to ditch it, to spare Infantino the embarrassment of acknowledging that his fake prize was really just a fake prize all along. Here is where we should probably acknowledge that, as fake prizes go, and in the context of what it was intended to accomplish, the first awarding of the Fifa peace prize was an unqualified success. It achieved exactly what it was meant to, made by Infantino to flatter Donald Trump, the man he needed to keep on his side to safeguard the riches to be extracted from the North American market in order to consolidate his power base within Fifa. Trump, the gullible buffoon, was pleased as punch – handed a big, golden bauble and a medal he placed around his own neck – and briefly forgot about the Nobel peace prize he desperately covets . Leander Schaerlaeckens is the author of The Long Game: US Men’s Soccer and Its Savage, Four-Decade Journey to the Top, or Thereabouts, which is out now . He teaches at Marist University. As Delap prepares to return to Ipswich, where his career ignited, on Friday night, Forest are remaining calm. There is a desperation to get away from the short-termism that caused so many problems; 12 months ago, they were on their third head coach of a disappointing season. This summer they were ruthless with the removal of Vítor Pereira, who had done a fine job to escape the drop, because they saw an opportunity to upgrade with Glasner, hoping he could transform Forest like he did Crystal Palace. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

Nothing erudite, anyway. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
